weight: An adjustable “importance” number on a connection. Training nudges it up or down so the network gets more answers right.
bias: A neuron’s built-in lean — how eager it is to fire before any input arrives. A positive bias leans YES, a negative bias leans NO.
sigmoid: A curve that squishes any number into the 0–1 range, so the output reads as a confidence.
neuron: The tiny machine: multiply each input by a weight, add the bias, then squish with an activation. One number comes out.
weighted sum: Every input times its weight, all added together (plus the bias). The single number that feeds into the activation.
activation: The “squisher” applied after the weighted sum — sigmoid, ReLU, and friends. It bends the line so the network can learn curves.
ReLU: A simple activation: keep positive numbers as-is, turn negatives into 0. Cheap to compute and the modern default.
softmax: Turns a list of scores into probabilities that add up to 1 — used when there are several possible answers.
gradient: The direction (and steepness) telling you how to change each weight to make the error smaller.
backpropagation: The bookkeeping that sends the error backward through the network to find each weight’s gradient.
learning rate: How big a step to take when nudging the weights. Too big overshoots; too small crawls.
epoch: One full pass through all of the training examples.
loss: A single number measuring how wrong the network is right now. Training tries to make it small.
overfitting: When a model memorizes the training examples instead of learning the general rule.
hidden neuron: A neuron in a middle layer — not an input, not the final output. Where the network builds its own features.
forward pass: Running inputs through the network to produce an output. No learning happens yet.
linearly separable: One straight line can split the YES examples from the NO examples. OR and AND are; XOR is not.
vector: Just a list of numbers, like [0.2, −1.4, 0.7].
matrix: A grid of numbers — a list of lists. One matrix multiply does many weighted sums at once.
dot product: Multiply the matching entries of two lists, then add them all up — the same multiply-and-add a neuron does.
token: A chunk of text (often a word-piece) with its own ID number. LLMs read and write tokens, not letters.
one-hot encoding: Writing a choice as a list with a single 1 and the rest 0s, like [0,1,0] for "chips".
tokenizer: The chopping rules plus a two-way lookup table between text chunks and id numbers. Built before training; never changes.
embedding: The row of learned numbers a token id looks up — the token’s numeric fingerprint.
